scope: Proposition 11.1 (Covariance estimates on most root orientations) of the manuscript “Critical mixing in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model” (preprints/Critical-mixing-in-the-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-model-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3ac6296cc238bae9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 46-47. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let S be suitable base orbit data retained by the preceding exclusions in Section 10. On S, use the disintegration dπ dHaar before the determinant weight w. Here dπ includes the scalar root factors and the imposed rotation-invariant spectral restriction, Haar is normalized measure on rotations fixing P, and w0 is the median reference weight defined there. 46 Fix 1/2 < γ < 1 and positive accuracies ϵ, η, together with the requested implied small constants below. Choose a sufficiently small fixed rate aorb > 0, then the upper bound on r sufficiently small. At each scale k = nr3 ≥ log10 n, for sufficiently large n, one may discard a further set E ⊆ S satisfying Z E w0 dπ ≤ CnC e−aorbk . On each remaining orbit, a set of Haar orientations of mass > 3/4 satisfies simultaneously ∥Σs∥ ≤ (1 + ϵ)/s, ∥A0ΣsA0∥ ≪ r−γ , ∥mpost s − m∥ ≪ r−1−η , ∥A0(mpost s − m)∥ ≪ r−γ/2 . (11.1) Here mpost s and Σs are the posterior mean and covariance. Every implied small constant can be prescribed in advance by shrinking the upper bound on r and then taking n sufficiently large. The previously excluded unsuitable data retain their preceding integrated bounds; w0 is used only on S. No bound uniform conditional on each spectrum is asserted.
